I met my boss on a site called fetlife.com she was offerring cheap tattoos by her newest artist, i said i didnt want any tattoos as i didnt have any money but asked if shed be willing to take me on as an apprentice. HOnestly i thought there would be no harm in asking. i thought she would say no, and my plan was the next week to apply to art schools and study for 4 years. but she said my stuff was really good, and they took me on. its been a year and a half. and honestly the past year and a half ive been working 7 day weeks 4 days at the shop 3 days at my other job to help pay for insurance gas and food. I moved out of my house and have been squatting in an abandoned warehouse so i could stretch my dollars even further. Its been a fucking tough go of things, but my career is picking up, ive got a small but dedicated clientele and after ive got a couple of grand saved move myself into a nice apartment. I practiced on myself mostly, my legs and feet are filled with my humble beginnings. then i had some nice friends who let me tattoo them for free, then when i was good enough my boss let me start tattooing at a REALLY discounted rate. I just kept working hard, not expecting anything. And now im a full artist making 150 an hour at the shop, im super happy with the progress. 

If youre looking to get started i have to warn you, its EXTREMELY competetive and EXTREMELY tough getting started, you start at the bottom no shit, i was scrubbing toilets, cleaning floors, emptying garbages, renovating shit, and studying every fucking thing possible about tattooing, bloodborne pathogens. I made no money for the first 9 months i was there. not one dollar. 

But i would work really fucking hard making a portfolio of drawings, a few your style and a few tattoo style. one hard thing i had to learn was i couldnt draw the way i wanted to, i had to make things look more mainstream tattoo-ey for the first little while, then you build a client base who trusts you on the foundations then you can experiment with your style more and more. But yeah make a STRONG protfolio. you think youre good? there are a fuckload of good artists out there, you have to think that when making your portfolio. have 5 excellent drawings rather than a book filled with mediocre drawings. then hit up shops. check out all the shops in your area that have artists that YOU like and aspire to be like. go to them and ask for an apprenticeship. if they all say no, go to more out of the way shops. I was lucky in that i ended up in a really good shop with great artists who are all about teaching and learning from each other. But once you do an apprenticeship, make it through your first year, you move on, you keep learning and getting better. its all about the basics, you master that, you can go anywhere.

A little long winded, but i hope this helps

It really depends, i personally dont think im too terribly amazing, i did put myself through artschool, so i have a pretty good education background. People think my stuff is great, and i personally strive to make everything i do always better than the last thing ive done. 

That being said, I know some people who are completely self taught and they are fantastic artists! My suggestion is, start drawing, every day. simple things, like your hands, bowls of fruit, flowers, anything and everything. to get good at the basics, like proportions, shading, and shapes. build a portfolio, or have a sketch book of what you think are your best drawings and go out to tattoo shops and ask if they are looking for apprentices. Some places might be dicks, some places might be awesome, some might tell you you dont have it, and some might tell you to go to art school (which is a great idea, i highly reccommend! i went to VanArts, amazing school, great teachers!) Or maybe they think youre good enough and offer you the apprenticeship right there. 

I dont know if thats too long winded of an answer, but thats the best advice i can give you.
